summary: Adds an email search filter to the user index, a self-service profile update endpoint, a user delete endpoint, and a welcome email callback on the User model.

findings.title: Search filter interpolates request input into SQL
findings.problem: The index action puts params[:q] straight into the LIKE clause text. Any quote in q ends the string literal and adds caller-controlled SQL.
findings.consequence: Any authenticated user can read or change arbitrary database rows, including other users' API tokens.
findings.fix: Bind q as a parameter and escape LIKE wildcards with sanitize_sql_like.

findings.title: Any user can delete any user
findings.problem: The change adds destroy to the require_admin exception list on line 2. The destroy action then deletes whatever record params[:id] names, with no ownership or role check.
findings.consequence: Any holder of a valid API token can delete every account, including admin accounts.
findings.fix: Remove destroy from the require_admin exception list so only admins reach this action.

findings.title: Profile update permits every attribute
findings.problem: The profile action permits every key in the user params, so any column is accepted. A caller can set admin or api_token on their own record.
findings.consequence: Any authenticated user can make themselves an admin and pass require_admin.
findings.fix: Permit only the fields a user may edit, such as email.

findings.title: Welcome email sent on every save
findings.problem: The after_save callback runs on updates as well as creates. Every profile update or other save therefore queues another welcome email.
findings.consequence: Existing users receive repeated welcome emails whenever their record changes.
findings.fix: Use after_create_commit so the mail goes out once, after the insert commits.

findings.title: New endpoints have no covering tests
findings.problem: The change adds search, profile and destroy behaviour plus a model callback. No test file exists in the repository to exercise them.
findings.consequence: Regressions in authorization and filtering will go unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add request specs for search, profile update, destroy authorization and the welcome email callback.
